tips.シ|ツ: シ: the short strokes sit on the left, one above the other, and the long stroke goes from bottom to top. ツ: the short strokes sit side by side at the top, and the long stroke goes from top to bottom.
tips.ソ|ン: ソ: the short stroke is fairly vertical and the long stroke runs from top to bottom. ン: the short stroke is fairly horizontal and the long stroke runs from bottom to top.
tips.ソ|ノ: ソ has an extra short stroke at the top left; ノ is a single stroke.
tips.ノ|ン: ン has an extra short stroke on the left; ノ is a single stroke.
tips.ぬ|め: ぬ ends with a small loop at the bottom right; め does not.
tips.ね|れ: Same left half. ね ends with a loop, れ with a flick outwards.
tips.ね|わ: Same left half. ね ends with a loop, わ with a round curve and no loop.
tips.れ|わ: Same left half. れ ends with a flick outwards, わ with a round curve.
tips.る|ろ: る has a loop at the bottom; ろ is open at the bottom.
tips.さ|ち: Mirror images: in ち the lower curve bulges to the right (like a 5), in さ to the left.
tips.き|さ: き has two horizontal strokes, さ only one.
tips.は|ほ: ほ has an extra horizontal stroke at the top right that closes off the vertical stroke. は is open at the top.
tips.け|は: は has a loop at the bottom right; け does not.
tips.け|ほ: ほ has two horizontal strokes on the right and a loop at the bottom; け has neither.
tips.ほ|ま: ほ has an extra vertical stroke on the left; ま does not.
tips.い|り: In り the right stroke is much longer and sweeps downwards.
tips.あ|お: お has a small extra stroke at the top right; あ does not.
tips.あ|め: あ has a horizontal stroke at the top; め does not.
tips.あ|ぬ: あ has a horizontal stroke at the top; ぬ ends with a loop.
tips.た|な: た: two short strokes on the right, like こ. な: a small stroke on the right and a loop at the bottom.
tips.う|ら: う has a horizontal stroke at the top and a round belly; ら has only a short slanted stroke at the top.
tips.ち|ら: ち has a full horizontal stroke at the top; ら only a short one.
tips.こ|に: に has an extra vertical stroke on the left; こ does not.
tips.ク|ケ: In ケ the horizontal stroke sticks out on the right. ク has only two strokes.
tips.ク|タ: タ is ク with an extra short stroke in the middle.
tips.ケ|タ: タ has a short stroke inside; in ケ the horizontal stroke sticks out on the right.
tips.コ|ユ: In ユ the bottom stroke sticks out at the sides; コ is an open bracket.
tips.コ|ロ: ロ is closed; コ is open on the left.
tips.ユ|ロ: ロ is a closed square; in ユ the bottom stroke sticks out.
tips.ウ|ワ: ウ has an extra short stroke on top; ワ does not.
tips.フ|ワ: ワ has a vertical stroke on the left; フ does not.
tips.ウ|フ: ウ has a short stroke on top and a vertical stroke on the left; フ has neither.
tips.チ|テ: In チ the vertical stroke crosses the horizontal one. テ has two horizontal strokes with the last stroke hanging below them.
tips.ナ|メ: ナ has a horizontal stroke; メ is made of two slanted strokes that cross.
tips.マ|ム: マ: a horizontal stroke with a hook at the top. ム: a sharp angle at the bottom with a small stroke on the right.
tips.ア|マ: In ア a long stroke runs from the middle down to the left; in マ a short stroke runs down to the right.
tips.ア|ム: ア: horizontal at the top with a long stroke down to the left. ム: a sharp angle at the bottom and a small stroke on the right.
tips.ス|ヌ: ヌ has an extra short stroke in the middle; ス does not.
tips.ル|レ: ル has an extra stroke on the left; レ is a single stroke.
tips.サ|セ: サ has two vertical strokes through the horizontal one; セ has only one, which curves out to the right at the bottom.
tips.フ|ヲ: ヲ has an extra horizontal stroke in the middle; フ does not.
tips.ニ|ミ: ニ: two horizontal strokes. ミ: three slanted strokes.
tips.木|本: 本 is 木 with an extra short stroke at the bottom of the trunk.
tips.休|木: 休 has an extra person (亻) on the left; 木 stands alone.
tips.日|目: 日 has one stroke inside, 目 has two and is narrower and taller.
tips.日|白: 白 is 日 with a short stroke on top.
tips.人|入: 人: the left stroke is longer. 入: the right stroke is longer.
tips.人|八: 人 is joined at the top, 八 is open at the top.
tips.十|千: 千 has an extra short slanted stroke at the top.
tips.右|石: 右 has a cross (ナ) on top, 石 a horizontal stroke with a slanted one below.
tips.右|左: They differ at the bottom: 右 has a mouth (口), 左 a tool (工).
tips.玉|王: 玉 is 王 with a dot at the bottom right.
tips.大|犬: 犬 is 大 with a dot at the top right.
tips.大|天: 天 is 大 with an extra horizontal stroke at the very top.
tips.子|字: 字 is 子 under a roof (宀).
tips.田|町: 町 has a street (丁) to the right of the field (田).
tips.林|森: 林: two trees. 森: three trees.
tips.上|下: 上: the vertical stroke stands above the line. 下: it hangs below.
tips.口|四: 四 is a box with two strokes inside, 口 is empty.

t.daku_tip: The two dashes ゛ make the sound voiced: k → g, s → z, t → d, h → b. The small circle ゜ turns h into p.
t.yoon_tip: The small character sets the vowel: ゃ/ャ = ya, ゅ/ュ = yu, ょ/ョ = yo.
t.hint_daku_rev_handaku: Look for a character with the small circle ゜. The circle turns the breathy sound of the H row into a hard lip sound.
t.hint_daku_rev: Look for a character with the two dashes ゛. Think of the base character with the voiceless partner sound: g ↔ k, z ↔ s, d ↔ t, b ↔ h.
t.hint_handaku: Base character: %1$s. The small circle ゜ turns the breathy h sound into a hard lip sound.
t.hint_daku: Base character: %1$s. The two dashes ゛ make the first sound voiced, that is, softer.
t.hint_yoon_rev: Look for a character ending in i plus a small ゃ, ゅ or ょ (or ャ, ュ, ョ). The small character sets the final vowel.
t.hint_yoon: Made of %1$s and a small %2$s. Say both in one go and drop the i in between.
t.table_prefix: In the table it is here:
t.table_alone: It stands alone in the last row of the table, after %1$s and %2$s.
t.rule_sokuon: The small っ/ッ doubles the next consonant: がっこう = gakkou (before ch: tch, e.g. ちょっと = chotto).
t.rule_choon: The bar ー lengthens the vowel before it: コーヒー = koohii.
t.kanji_hint_strokes: The kanji you need has %1$d strokes.

あ: On the left a cross like a pharmacy sign, on the right a wide-open round mouth. What do you say when the doctor looks down your throat?
い: Two earthworms lying side by side in the grass. What do you shout when you have to pick them up?
う: A small head on top and a bent body below, clutching its stomach. What do you groan with a stomach ache?
え: A small sign on top and someone below running off with one leg kicked back. What does the green sign above the door say?
お: A cross, a round belly and a splash flying off at the top right. What do you gasp when you spill food on yourself?
か: A fighter with a bent arm and a short strike line next to him. Which Japanese martial art is fought with empty hands?
き: It looks like an old door opener with two teeth that you turn in a lock. What is it called?
く: An open beak seen from the side. Which bird calls its own name, even from a clock?
け: On the left a tap, on the right a barrel on its stand. What is a small beer barrel called?
こ: Two strokes, one above the other, like two players gaming together. What is playing together in a game called?
さ: A warrior bowing deeply with his sword held across. What is a Japanese sword fighter called?
し: One long strand of hair hanging down and curling up at the end. Who has hair like that – he or …?
す: A loop hanging from a chopstick. Which Japanese dish is made of rice and raw fish?
せ: A crossbar as a backrest with a raised seat below. An old word for a small sofa.
そ: A zigzag, as if someone were drizzling gravy over a plate. What is poured over the food?
た: On the left a tall dancer with an arm stretched out, on the right two small steps. Which Argentinian dance is it?
ち: A collar (the crossbar) over a small round belly. The tiniest dog in the world, from Mexico.
つ: One single giant wave rolling in. Everyone knows the Japanese word for it.
て: A hand reaching out from a horizontal arm. How many fingers do two hands have?
と: A splinter stuck at an angle in your big … what?
な: A cross, a crumb and a twisted loop of melted cheese. Which Mexican snack?
に: On the left a leg, on the right two plasters. Which joint do you scrape when you fall?
ぬ: Twisted loops with a knot at the end, like long pasta on a fork.
ね: A thread looping into a little knot. Fishermen need lots of them for their …
の: A circle with a slash through it, like a prohibition sign. What does it say?
は: A stroke on the left, someone on the right doubled over with laughter. What does laughter sound like?
ひ: A wide, sly grin. How do you giggle?
ふ: Four strokes like a summit with clouds drifting past. Japan’s most famous volcano.
へ: A low pointed arch, like a hard hat seen from the side. What protects your head on a bike?
ほ: On the left a chimney, on the right a man with a big belly. How does Santa laugh?
ま: Two outstretched arms and a round belly below with a baby inside. Who is a baby’s first word?
み: A curled tail and a whisker sticking out. What does the cat say?
む: A cow with a loop for an udder and a horn (the small stroke on the right). What does it say?
め: A round fruit with a cross cut into it. Big, green outside, juicy inside.
も: A fishing hook with two worms on it. The greedy angler still wants …
や: A big curved horn sticking up next to a short stroke. A shaggy ox from the Himalayas.
ゆ: A round body with a long straight horn right through the middle. A magical horse.
よ: A disc on a string, zooming up and down. Which toy?
ら: A short ear on top and a round body below that hops away. Which animal?
り: A short and a very tall stroke side by side, like reeds on a bank. Where do reeds grow?
る: A road that ends in a loop at the bottom, like a roundabout. What do you call the way you take?
れ: A post on the left, on the right a runner sprinting off and handing something over. A team race with a baton.
ろ: Like a 3 whose lower belly is open: something has fallen out. What does a ball do down a hill?
わ: A post on the left and a wave lapping against it on the right. What is the wave made of?
を: Someone throws up an arm in surprise. What does a rider shout to stop a horse?
ん: The only character without a vowel. It sounds like a thoughtful hum with your mouth closed.
ア: A wide blade on top and a slanted handle below. Used to chop wood.
イ: A spear glances off a post. Whoever stands next to it squeaks …
ウ: Like the hiragana with the same reading, but with a lid on top. What do you say when something amazes you?
エ: One floor above the other, connected by a shaft. What takes you up?
オ: A cross with a slanted stroke, like someone leaning forward on a walking stick. A very … man.
カ: A bent paddle with a grip. Used for a narrow boat you sit in.
キ: A door opener with two teeth that you turn in a lock. What is it called?
ク: A wedge cut from a big round biscuit, seen from the side.
ケ: A spout sticking out to the left and a handle on top. It boils water.
コ: Two lines meeting at square angles, open on the left, like where two walls meet. What is that called?
サ: A wooden bench on two legs where you sweat in the heat.
シ: Two little eyes on the left and a long smile sweeping upwards: a girl winking at you. Who is it?
ス: A heavy Japanese wrestler standing with his legs wide apart.
セ: A table top with a hooked edge and one bent leg. Before dinner you … the table.
ソ: Two drops fall from above, the second one long and thick like gravy.
タ: A folded shell with a filling inside. Which Mexican dish?
チ: A pod with a curved stem and two ridges. Very hot!
ツ: Two drops side by side at the top, and the long stroke crashes down: a giant wave breaks. Everyone knows the Japanese word for it.
テ: A pole with two crossbars at the top. Wires for calls used to hang on it.
ト: A tall pole with a small wing sticking out. A carved … pole.
ナ: A cross with a long, slightly bent tusk. Which whale has a single tusk?
ニ: Two strokes, one above the other, like two bent legs. Which joint bends there?
ヌ: A chopstick (the short stroke) fishing in a bowl for long pasta.
ネ: A small bird on top and a woven bundle of twigs below: its home in the tree.
ノ: A single slash, like a prohibition sign without the circle. What does it say?
ハ: Two slanted strokes like a pointed top without a brim. What do you wear on your head?
ヒ: A donkey’s head with one ear sticking up. What sound does it make?
フ: A spoon seen from the side, bent at the top left. What goes on it?
ヘ: The same in both scripts: a low pointed arch like a hard hat seen from the side.
ホ: A Christmas tree with a trunk and two branches. How does the man in the red coat laugh?
マ: A mouth forming the very first word of many babies.
ミ: Three whiskers. What does the animal say?
ム: A wide cow’s nose with one nostril (the small stroke). What does the animal say?
メ: An X like the kiss at the end of a text. What did you just send?
モ: A hook with two crossbars, like a square fishing hook. The angler wants …
ヤ: A shaggy ox with one big curved horn, from the Himalayas.
ユ: A flat hull with a deck line, gliding under the sea. A German submarine.
ヨ: Three bars like stacked mats. Stretching and breathing exercises.
ラ: A lid over a curved bowl of Japanese noodle soup.
リ: A short and a very tall stroke, like reeds growing on a bank. Where do they grow?
ル: Two sticks leaning against each other, the right one kinked outwards. Used to measure lines.
レ: A check mark next to every ingredient. On which sheet does it say how to cook?
ロ: A square box: the head of a tin machine.
ワ: A small dish with a high rim on the left holding a green paste for sushi.
ヲ: A signpost with two arms. What does a rider shout to stop the horse?
ン: A short stroke and a long one rising from the bottom. It sounds like a thoughtful hum with your mouth closed.

kh.二: Horizontal strokes, one more than 一.
kh.三: Horizontal strokes, one more than 二.
kh.五: Two lines with a zigzag between them.
kh.六: A roof with two little legs beneath.
kh.七: A cross with a foot bent to the right.
kh.九: An arm bending far round: one short of ten.
kh.十: A cross like a plus sign.
kh.千: Ten (十) with a stroke on top.
kh.円: An open frame, like the coin tray of a till.
kh.日: A frame with a line in the middle, like a disc in the sky.
kh.月: A narrow crescent with two lines inside.
kh.火: Flames licking upwards with sparks to the left and right.
kh.水: A stream with splashes on both sides.
kh.木: A trunk with branches and roots.
kh.金: Under a roof, grains glitter in the earth.
kh.土: A small mound on a long line.
kh.山: Three peaks, the middle one highest.
kh.田: A plot divided into four parts.
kh.空: A hole (穴) above work (工): high up there is nothing.
kh.天: A big person (大) with a stroke above the head.
kh.雨: A cloud under the sky with drops falling out.
kh.夕: Half a moon (月 missing a stroke): it is just rising.
kh.早: The sun (日) just above the horizon (十).
kh.年: A person carrying the ripe harvest on their back: once each cycle.
kh.子: A baby in swaddling clothes with arms spread out.
kh.女: A kneeling figure with arms crossed.
kh.男: A rice field (田) and strength (力): the one working the field.
kh.王: Three levels (heaven, people, earth) joined by one stroke: the ruler.
kh.玉: The king (王) with a small dot: his treasure.
kh.口: An open square that talks and eats.
kh.目: An upright oval with two lid lines.
kh.耳: A shell-like shape with folds on the side of the head.
kh.手: Five fingers: three crossbars and a curved stem.
kh.力: A tensed arm with a muscle.
kh.上: A line with something standing on top of it.
kh.下: A line with something hanging underneath it.
kh.中: A stroke right through a box.
kh.大: A person stretching arms and legs wide.
kh.小: A stroke in the middle and two tiny dots beside it.
kh.左: A hand above a tool (工): the hand that holds.
kh.右: A hand above a mouth (口): the hand you eat with.
kh.先: A foot stepping forward over two legs.
kh.生: A sprout growing out of the earth (土).
kh.正: A foot (止) stops under the line: exactly on target.
kh.立: A person upright on the ground.
kh.見: A big eye (目) on two legs.
kh.休: A person (亻) leaning against a tree (木).
kh.出: Two mountains stacked: a sprout breaking through the ground.
kh.入: An arrow slipping into a gap.
kh.音: Someone stands (立) above a sun (日) and hears something.
kh.名: Evening (夕) and mouth (口): in the dark you call out this.
kh.字: A child (子) under a roof (宀) learns to write.
kh.学: A child (子) under a roof onto which knowledge falls.
kh.校: A tree (木) beside crossed legs (交): where everyone meets to learn.
kh.文: A person with a pattern on the chest: written signs.
kh.本: A tree (木) with a mark at the root.
kh.花: Plants (⺾) on top, something changing (化) below: it opens up.
kh.貝: A case like an eye on two little legs; long ago it was used as money.
kh.犬: Big (大) with a dot: the ear of a loyal pet.
kh.虫: A head (口) with a body and feelers.
kh.糸: A twisted strand, pulled apart at the bottom.
kh.車: Seen from above: a box on an axle with two wheels.
kh.町: Rice fields (田) and a street (丁).
kh.村: Trees (木) and a hand (寸): a few houses among the green.
kh.白: The sun (日) with a ray of light on top.
kh.青: A young sprout (生) above the moon (月): the colour of a clear sky.
kh.赤: Earth (土) over flames: a glowing colour.
